source_text:
Ὁ ἄρχων τοῦ αἰῶνος τούτου διαρπάσαι με βούλεται καὶ τὴν εἰς θεόν μου γνώμην διαφθεῖραι. μηδεὶς οὖν τῶν παρόντων ὑμῶν βοηθείτω αὐτῷ: μᾶλλον ἐμοῦ γίνεσθε, τουτέστιν τοῦ θεοῦ. μὴ λαλεῖτε Ἰησοῦν Χριστόν, κόσμον δὲ ἐπιθυμεῖτε.
βασκανία ἐν ὑμῖν μὴ κατοικείτω. μηδ’ ἂν ἐγὼ παρὼν παρακαλῶ ὑμᾶς, πείσθητέ μοι: τούτοις δὲ μᾶλλον πείσθητε, οἷς γράφω ὑμῖν. ζῶν γὰρ γράφω ὑμῖν, ἐρῶν τοῦ ἀποθανεῖν. ὁ ἐμὸς ἔρως ἐσταύρωται, καὶ οὐκ ἔστιν ἐν ἐμοὶ πῦρ φιλόυλον: ὕδωρ δὲ ζῶν καὶ λαλοῦν ἐν ἐμοί, ἔσωθέν μοι λέγον: Δεῦρο πρὸς τὸν πατέρα.
οὐχ ἥδομαι τροφῇ φθορᾶς οὐδὲ ἡδοναῖς τοῦ βίου τούτου. ἄρτον θεοῦ θέλω, ὅ ἐστιν σὰρξ Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ, τοῦ ἐκ σπέρματος Δαυείδ, καὶ πόμα θέλω τὸ αἷμα αὐτοῦ, ὅ ἐστιν ἀγάπη ἄφθαρτος.
thought_title: The ruler of this age wants to destroy me; my love is crucified
orientation: Ignatius, bishop of Antioch, is writing to the Roman church while being taken under guard to Rome, where he expects to be martyred by wild beasts, and he is urging them not to prevent his death.
pass_a_gloss: The ruler of this age wants to snatch me away and to corrupt my purpose toward God. Therefore let none of you who are present help him; rather become mine, that is, God's. Do not speak Jesus Christ, and desire the world. Let envy not dwell in you. And not even if I, being present, urge you, be persuaded by me; but be persuaded rather by these things which I write to you. For I write to you living, longing to die. My love is crucified, and there is not in me a fire that loves matter; but living water and speaking in me, saying within me: Come to the Father. I do not delight in food of corruption nor in the pleasures of this life. I want the bread of God, which is the flesh of Jesus Christ, who is from the seed of David, and I want as drink his blood, which is incorruptible love.

lemmas.gloss: to delight in, take pleasure in

choices.why: Fixed glossary rendering for the devil, the ruler of this present age
Ignatius's settled intention toward God, not merely an opinion
The context of urging the Romans not to hinder his martyrdom suggests malicious envy or ill-will, not just general malice
The participle expresses passionate desire, matching the following statement that his love is crucified
Keeps the perfect tense and the stark metaphor of Ignatius's earthly desires being put to death with Christ
The adjective describes a fire attached to material things, contrasting with the living water within him

bible_refs.note: ἄρτον θεοῦ θέλω, ὅ ἐστιν σὰρξ Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ — bread of God which is the flesh of Jesus Christ
πόμα θέλω τὸ αἷμα αὐτοῦ — his blood as drink

pass_b_english: The ruler of this age wants to seize me and corrupt my purpose toward God. So let none of you who are present help him. Instead, take my side, which is God's side. Do not speak the name of Jesus Christ while you long for the world.

Let no envy dwell among you. And even if I, when I am present, urge you otherwise, do not be persuaded by me. Be persuaded instead by what I am writing to you. For I write to you while I am alive, longing to die. My earthly love has been crucified, and there is no fire in me that longs for material things. But living water is speaking within me, and from inside me it says: "Come to the Father."

I take no pleasure in the food of corruption or in the pleasures of this life. I want the bread of God, which is the flesh of Jesus Christ, who is from the seed of David, and I want his blood as drink, which is incorruptible love.

last_rejected.quote: Do not speak Jesus Christ while you long for the world.
last_rejected.source_quote: μὴ λαλεῖτε Ἰησοῦν Χριστόν, κόσμον δὲ ἐπιθυμεῖτε.
last_rejected.why: Greek contrasts not speaking of Christ with desiring the world; English adds a temporal clause linking the two, changing the contrast.
last_rejected.fix: Do not speak of Jesus Christ, but desire the world.
last_rejected.ruling: μὴ...δὲ naturally renders as 'Do not...while...' or 'Do not...but'; 'while' preserves the contrast adequately.

polish.changed: Clarified speaker and pronoun references, smoothed sentence order, and preserved all claims and quotations while making the metaphors readable aloud.

notes.why: Famous crux; meaning obscure (worldly affections dead? love nailed to cross?).
notes.fix: Add interpretive note on possible meanings.

notes.quote: there is no fire in me that loves matter
notes.why: 'Fire that loves matter' is philosophically technical (Stoic?); unexplained.
notes.fix: Note: 'Ignatius denies materialist desire, using philosophical language for elemental fire.'

notes.quote: there is no fire in me that loves matter
notes.why: Opaque metaphor; reader cannot tell what 'fire loving matter' means.
notes.fix: Clarify: 'no earthly passion burns in me for material things.'

polish.changed: Clarified the compressed paradox about crucified love and material desire, and made the living water's speech flow naturally while keeping every claim and quotation intact.

notes.quote: My love is crucified, and there is no fire in me that loves matter.
notes.why: Compressed paradox: 'my love is crucified' = my earthly affections are dead? 'fire that loves matter' = material desires? Obscure without explanation.
notes.fix: Add note explaining 'my love is crucified' as 'my earthly desires are crucified/dead'.

notes.quote: there is living water speaking within me
notes.why: 'Living water' is Johannine metaphor for Spirit, but 'speaking within me' personifies it unusually.

polish.changed: Clarified that the living water speaking within Ignatius is an interior voice, and resolved the ambiguous 'earthly love' to 'love for earthly things' so the metaphor of crucified desire reads naturally.

notes.why: Presented as 'living water speaking within me,' i.e., Christ/Spirit; reader may miss this is interior locution.
notes.fix: Identify as words of 'living water' (Christ/Spirit) within Ignatius.

notes.quote: My earthly love has been crucified, and there is no fire in me that longs for material things.
notes.why: 'Earthly love' and 'fire' are mixed metaphors; 'fire' for desire is biblical but abrupt here.
notes.fix: Acceptable with note; or 'the fire of earthly desire has been extinguished.'

notes.quote: My earthly love has been crucified
notes.why: 'Earthly love' (philēma or similar) could mean 'my beloved' (person) or 'my love for earthly things'; ambiguous.
notes.fix: Note: likely means 'my love for earthly things has been crucified.'

notes.why: Not exact citation but alludes to John 14:6, 16:28; 'living water' from John 4:10, 7:38.
notes.fix: Note as conflated Johannine allusion, not direct quotation.

polish.changed: Clarified that the living water is the speaker of the inner call to the Father, made the pronoun references explicit, and smoothed the sentence flow for reading aloud while preserving every claim and quotation.

notes.why: Words of 'living water speaking within me'—reader may not recognize this as a quotation or allusion to John 4:14 or 7:38.
notes.fix: Add note identifying this as an allusion to Johannine 'living water' passages.

notes.quote: living water speaking within me, saying to me from inside: "Come to the Father."
notes.why: Reader may not know if 'living water' is the Spirit, Christ, or a scriptural allusion (John 4:10; 7:38).
notes.fix: Note the allusion to John's Gospel or identify the speaker as the Spirit.

polish.changed: Clarified that 'my love' refers to Ignatius's earthly love, and identified the living water as the Spirit speaking within him, while preserving all claims and quotations exactly.

notes.why: Striking but opaque: his earthly affections? His love for Christ? Greek 'agape' = love or beloved?
notes.fix: Gloss: 'my [earthly] love has been crucified' or 'my beloved [life] is crucified.'

notes.quote: living water is speaking within me, and from inside me it says: "Come to the Father."
notes.why: Reader may not know if 'living water' is the Spirit, Christ, or Ignatius's own inner voice.
notes.fix: Clarify that 'living water' likely refers to the Spirit or divine voice within.

problems.quote: But there is living water speaking within me, and from inside me it says: "Come to the Father."
problems.why: Unclear whether this is Ignatius's own thought, the Spirit, or allusion to Scripture (John 4:10, 7:38).
problems.fix: Add note identifying as likely allusion to Johannine 'living water' or prophetic experience.

problems.quote: My love for earthly things has been crucified
problems.why: Poetic but compressed; 'love' as subject of crucifixion is personification reader may find odd.
problems.fix: Add note or rephrase: 'My desire for earthly things has been crucified [i.e., put to death] with Christ.'

problems.quote: there is living water speaking within me, and from inside me it says: "Come to the Father."

problems.fix: Clarify the source of the voice.
